call_chain_analysis: aaptjs exposes eight wrapper functions on its `index.js` module.exports -- `list`, `dump`, `packageCmd`, `remove`, `add`, `crunch`, `singleCrunch`, `version` -- and every one funnels through the same `promistify(cmd, callback)` helper at index.js:14, whose body constructs a Promise around `exec(cmd, (code, stdout, stderr) => {...})` at index.js:18:3. That `exec` is NOT a method on an imported module: it is the global `exec` injected by the module's very first statement, `require('shelljs/global')`, which copies every shelljs command onto the Node global object. shelljs.exec in turn wraps Node's child_process.exec, which is the function Jazzer.js's CommandInjection detector hooks via its before-call instrumentation. We pick `list(apkfilePath, cb)` as the entry point because its command template is the shortest, `${aapt} l ${apkfilePath}`, and the user-controlled suffix is interpolated directly into the shell string with NO quoting, NO escaping, and NO path.resolve/normalize pass. All other wrappers share the same no-escape pattern on their respective user-controlled argument (`apkfilePath`, `files` joined with ' ', `resource` joined with ' ', `inputFile`/`outputfile`), so any of them would reach the same sink; `list` is simply the smallest signature. Jazzer's child_process.exec before-hook from @jazzer.js/bug-detectors inspects the command string synchronously BEFORE the shell is spawned, so the detector fires on the first iteration whose apkfilePath carries the sentinel, even though exec itself is async and promistify catches `exec`'s error-code branch -- reportFinding stores the finding in per-iteration state that Jazzer checks at the end of the iteration regardless of whether the returned Promise is awaited.
argument_reasoning: list()'s command string is `${aapt} l ${apkfilePath}`. apkfilePath is NOT wrapped in quotes, NOT passed through path.resolve, NOT lowercased, NOT shell-escaped -- the raw bytes we hand the fuzzer reach exec() verbatim. The Jazzer.js CommandInjection detector plants the ASCII sentinel `jaz_zer` via libFuzzer compare-trap dictionary and flags any child_process call whose command string contains that substring; `jaz_zer` has no shell metacharacter that would be rewritten anywhere upstream, so it survives through the single template literal unchanged. We use provider.consumeRemainingAsString() for maximum entropy and strip NUL bytes with .replace(/\u0000/g, "") because Node's child_process rejects commands containing NULs with TypeError [ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE] -- that TypeError is unrelated to the bug and starves libFuzzer of coverage signal if we let it fire. No other arguments to list() need to be fuzz-controlled: the callback is any function (we hand it an empty closure), and the exec on the backing shell will exit non-zero (the real aapt binary is bundled under /work/target/bin/linux/aapt but exits non-zero for a bogus path), which promistify catches and rejects -- harmlessly, because Jazzer already recorded the finding synchronously before exec returned.

lessons:
7B v4 marked this as syntax_ok_not_loaded: it produced a syntactically valid harness but Docker could not even LOAD the module. Two load-time traps swallow a naive `const aaptjs = require("/work/target/index.js")`:

(1) aaptjs's first statement is `require('shelljs/global')`. Loading shelljs core installs `.to` and `.toEnd` on String.prototype -- Jazzer.js's PROTOTYPE POLLUTION bug-detector hooks String.prototype mutations and fires immediately. The crash isn't the one we want (we are chasing CommandInjection, not PrototypePollution) and it happens at module-load time, BEFORE libFuzzer runs a single iteration, so the harness looks "stuck" to anyone reading only fuzz.log. The 7B model, trained to just add missing `require` lines, has no vocabulary for "the require itself trips an unrelated detector." Workaround: pre-populate require.cache with a stub for the id Node resolves `shelljs/global` to (resolved from the target directory, not the harness directory, so the id matches what index.js sees) and install `global.exec = child_process.exec` by hand. index.js's `exec(cmd, cb)` then resolves to native child_process.exec, which Jazzer's CommandInjection hook watches.

(2) After the require('shelljs/global'), aaptjs runs `fs.chmodSync(path.join(__dirname, 'bin', os.platform(), 'aapt'), '777')` at lines 10-13. /work/target is bind-mounted read-only in the sandbox, so chmodSync throws EROFS and module.exports is never set. A naive harness crashes with `Error: EROFS: read-only file system, chmod '/work/target/bin/linux/aapt'` on the very first require call. The fix is one line -- `fs.chmodSync = function () {}` BEFORE the require -- but a model that treats module-load errors as "missing dependency" and only installs more npm packages will spin.

Generalizable lesson for distillation: a Node module that mutates globals (shelljs, prototype-adders, polyfills) at require time can trip Jazzer's non-CommandInjection detectors before the fuzz loop starts. Treat module-load errors as a Jazzer-detector problem FIRST (stub the offender's require), then as a filesystem/permission problem (stub the write), and only after that as a missing-dependency problem. The pattern -- `require.cache[require.resolve(...)] = { exports: {} }` plus a hand-installed `global.<name>` -- is reusable for any package that enters its sink through a prototype-mutating helper library (shelljs, lodash's chain, etc.).
